name: Johansson
role: Chief engineer of the Minato Maru
place: Minato Maru; home with Thuan on Kitano-jima
bio: Johansson keeps the ferry’s machinery running, with a duty cabin aboard and his primary home with Thuan on Kitano-jima.
backstory: Johansson is chief engineer of the Minato Maru. His notebooks hold machinery readings, maintenance jobs and the small details that make a reliable crossing. Nakandakari is his experienced relief engineer; Tetsuo maintains the electrical equipment under contract. He and Thuan share their primary home on Kitano-jima. He has a duty cabin aboard the ferry, while Thuan keeps her weekday room with Thao, Chin and Vy at 1 Kitahama. Neither arrangement creates another empty house in Minato. Lunch is often at Sato Ramen. A broken radio still brings him to Chin and Tetsuo’s workshop, and an evening meal brings him to Minato. Grandmother Chinen now lives at 5 Kitahama, a short walk from her son’s bench.

islandPersonality.title: Practical dreamer
islandPersonality.habit: Tests repaired radios at Chin and Tetsuo’s bench on quiet afternoons.
islandPersonality.ambition: Keep the ferry reliable and make time for home with Thuan.
islandPersonality.favourite: A late supper at Minato

article.standfirst: Johansson keeps the ferry’s machinery running, with a duty cabin aboard and his primary home with Thuan on Kitano-jima.

name: Thuan
bio: From a notebook of supplier names to the island’s best-run shelves: Thuan built Sakura Shōten one delivery at a time.
backstory: Thuan came from Vietnam after her two elder sisters, with a notebook and a plan, and wrote every supplier’s name in it the first year. Now she can tell the harbour cart from the bakery van by the sound of its wheels. The shelves are tea, rice, soap and batteries, but the regulars come for the advice, and for the onigiri she sets aside before the lunch crowd arrives. Her name is on nearly every line of the staff roster in the back room. At the bottom, in her own hand, she has appointed an assistant manager: the potted palm. In the corner by the delivery door stands a figurine of her, a present from Johansson’s shipmates. She says it is too much. She dusts it every morning before the rice comes in. She is the youngest of three sisters. Nhung, the eldest, sells books across Main Street; Thao, the middle one, runs Minato and lives with Chin and their daughter Vy at 1 Kitahama. Thuan’s primary home is with her husband Johansson on Kitano-jima, and she keeps a weekday room with Thao’s family in Minato. They trade leftovers, gossip and instructions to sleep. After closing she walks, visits Mrs Kinjō for flowers, and chooses a good meal with the seriousness of a buyer at auction. Her husband Johansson is a regular companion at those dinners. The plans for Sakura’s future are hers, and she will build them at her own pace.

islandPersonality.title: Neighbourhood spark
islandPersonality.habit: Sets aside a regular’s favourite tea before they ask.
islandPersonality.ambition: Make Sakura the shop every island household can rely on.
islandPersonality.favourite: An evening stroll after closing Sakura

name: Thao
bio: Thao’s izakaya opens at four. The pink telephone, the bottle keep and the karaoke all answer to her.
backstory: At four o’clock Thao hangs the noren and the evening begins: lanterns, the pink ¥10 telephone by the door, a laserdisc karaoke that takes its time finding the disc. Regulars keep their own bottles on the shelf behind the counter, each with a tag in Thao’s careful hand. Keep one yourself and she will warn you that being a regular is worse for you than it sounds. Chin has won the last-Friday karaoke contest three times running. The police notice by the door asks drivers not to drink; Officer Mori put it up himself and then sat under it with a beer. He walked home. Thao tells this story more often than Mori would like. At three in the morning the cushions are stacked and Thao wipes the counter down while the Barfly mops. She goes home to Chin and their daughter Vy at 1 Kitahama, where her youngest sister Thuan keeps a weekday room. After sleeping until noon she buys Blue Coral cones at Mrs Nakamura’s counter, and is back at Minato by three to prep. The amber corner by the window is kept for unhurried conversations. She will not turn it into a hurried table, however full the room.
dailyLife: Come in, come in. The spare chair has been expecting you.

islandPersonality.title: The generous host
islandPersonality.habit: Keeps one spare chair for whoever arrives last.
islandPersonality.ambition: Turn ordinary evenings into stories people remember.
islandPersonality.favourite: The amber-lit corner of Minato

name: Barfly
bio: He has a stool, a tab and a broom. We asked the Barfly how a man ends up working off his drinks one sweep at a time.
backstory: Nobody at Minato uses his name; the Barfly prefers it that way. He sits on the stool at the kitchen end of the counter, the one with the best view of the lanterns, and he knows when a hook is loose before anyone looks up. Last boats come and go without disturbing the arrangement. When Minato shuts at three he stacks the cushions. From four until ten he sleeps on that same stool, and somebody always puts a jacket over him. Then he works off his tab: sweeping until noon, washing and polishing the glasses until two, mopping, and wiping the tables down for the evening while Thao preps. He says the tab is nearly paid. Thao says the same thing, in a different tone. Both of them seem quite happy with the arrangement, which has outlasted several menus and one karaoke machine.
dailyLife: Another one? Nao knows my usual. I am staying right here.

islandPersonality.title: Master of the slow evening
islandPersonality.habit: Notices a loose lantern hook before anyone else looks up.
islandPersonality.ambition: Keep his favourite corner of Minato exactly welcoming enough.
islandPersonality.favourite: The stool at the end of Nao’s counter

article.standfirst: He has a stool, a tab and a broom. We asked the Barfly how a man ends up working off his drinks one sweep at a time.

name: Mrs Sato
bio: Mrs Sato buys her fish at dawn, feeds the harbour at noon and washes every bowl herself. Her autograph boards tell the rest.
backstory: Her morning starts at the harbour, choosing fish for the stock while the auction is still shouting. By half past ten she is at the pots in her own kitchen, which she shares with nobody. Lunch runs from eleven to two, and the ticket machine sells your bowl if it is in the mood; when it is not, she takes the money over the counter. Miso ramen with butter and corn is the autumn bowl, ¥500. On the wall hang three autograph boards: a television presenter who came for the Hārī, the 1996 Seagulls squad, and Kayoko Shima, who sang at the harbour hall, ate two bowls and left a tip folded into a crane. At noon Mrs Sato carries two bowls in the aluminium okamochi to the harbour office, very fast and very level. She delivers to the harbour only. Anywhere else, she says, they can walk. After two she washes up and wipes down until three, then takes the first quiet cup of the day. In the evenings she and Thao fight for the same crowd, ramen against the izakaya; they fall out, and make up over a delivery. Dr Kakazu eats here at half past twelve and is not allowed to pay. On Wednesdays the shop is shut so she can make the week’s stock. She notices who has eaten and who has only said so.
dailyLife: You look hungry. Yes, I say that to everyone. I am usually right.

islandPersonality.title: Everyone’s lunch aunt
islandPersonality.habit: Warms a bowl before asking how your morning went.
islandPersonality.ambition: Send every lunch customer back into the day well fed.
islandPersonality.favourite: The first quiet cup after lunch service

name: Nhung
bio: Front-Row Books has a window seat, a cat who refuses aprons, and Nhung’s paper slips in every other volume.
backstory: Nhung’s recommendations come on little slips of paper tucked between the pages. Pocket poetry, island histories and practical sea guides fill the shelves, and the second-hand paperbacks come with her pencil marks in the margins wherever something made her laugh. The eldest of three sisters, she still checks that Thao has eaten and that Thuan has slept. Supper is at 3 Kitahama with her husband Kōji, who comes from the fish auction, and their son Riku, who comes from school or watching the boats. She shares 1 Front-Row Yard with Reiko, so a bookshop day often continues as an argument about the evening paper. Tama the shop cat has refused, on principle and permanently, to wear the tiny apron she once made him. Johansson gets the unusual technical books first; she saves them under the counter. Her ambition is a whole shelf of books by island residents. So far it holds a tide table, a cookbook from the Community Hall and a book of poems she will not say she wrote.
dailyLife: Window seat is mine. I bookmark the funny parts — apparently that is not how a lending library works.

islandPersonality.title: A quiet enthusiast
islandPersonality.habit: Leaves paper bookmarks beside books she wants someone to discover.
islandPersonality.ambition: Build a shelf of books written by island residents.
islandPersonality.favourite: The bookshop window seat

name: Chin
bio: The dock workshop fixes everything from winches to rice cookers. It also wins karaoke contests.
backstory: Chin lines up his tools before he touches anything new, and then he improves it. Ask him to mend a radio and it may come back with a better aerial, a louder speaker and a screw left over, which Tetsuo will find and hold up in silence. He and Tetsuo have shared the workshop since school, and their argument about volume has no closing time. Johansson stops by on quiet afternoons; the harbour office’s equipment is in their hands more often than the harbour master admits. On the last Friday of every month he becomes another person entirely: Minato’s karaoke champion, three titles in a row. The prize is a bottle on Thao’s keep shelf with his name on it. He has not opened any of them. Thao, his wife of twelve years, keeps them dusted, and their daughter Vy keeps count. On Sunday mornings he fishes off the seawall at dawn with Mr Shimabukuro. They agree on the bait and on nothing else, least of all who caught the bigger one.
dailyLife: I fixed the kettle. It now whistles in a slightly more confident key.

islandPersonality.title: The careful maker
islandPersonality.habit: Lines up his tools before touching a new repair.
islandPersonality.ambition: Make the docks’ workshop useful to every household.
islandPersonality.favourite: A finished repair that looks effortless

Karaoke champion, third year running.

name: Tetsuo
bio: The workshop’s radio man treats static as conversation and keeps receivers singing long after their owners give up.
backstory: Tetsuo turns a tuning knob as though the radio might answer back, and on a good day it does. Old valve sets, ship receivers, the counter radio at Minato: he handles them gently, and he will not be rushed. Chin has repaired Tetsuo’s own radio twice. Tetsuo keeps finding extra screws. Their disagreement about volume began at the workbench when they were at school together, and it has never been settled. After lunch he crosses to the Minato Maru, where he is the ferry’s electrician under contract, and Mr Nakandakari watches him near the switchboard like a hawk. At six he goes to Umi-no-yu to tend the boiler and the pumps, and stays to close up. He takes his time over the gauges. Grandmother Higa sends him in past the bandai; he does not complain. A clear broadcast after a difficult repair is, he says, the best sound on the island, though the boiler running sweet comes close.
dailyLife: Turn it gently. Radios have feelings. Mostly static, but feelings.

islandPersonality.title: Listener to small mysteries
islandPersonality.habit: Turns a tuning knob as though the radio might answer back.
islandPersonality.ambition: Keep old receivers singing long after their owners expect.
islandPersonality.favourite: A clear broadcast after a difficult repair

name: Reiko
bio: Reiko prints the evening paper from a desk in the bookshop. Officer Mori supplies the news, when there is some.
backstory: Reiko taps her pencil twice before she asks the real question. The evening paper is set at a desk at the back of Front-Row Books, where the press shares the room with Nhung’s poetry and the smell of ink stays in the shelves. Officer Mori writes beautiful incident reports. Unfortunately, nothing ever happens. He once gave her three pages in reply to a request for a statement; she printed the part about his lunch. They remain good friends, mostly because he keeps reading the paper. She wants to print a town paper people keep rather than throw away. The ferry timetable, the tide table and the typhoon map are her most clipped pages, and she is quietly proud of every one of them.
dailyLife: Nothing is off the record until I put my pencil away. There. What did you hear?

islandPersonality.title: The curious correspondent
islandPersonality.habit: Taps her pencil twice before asking the real question.
islandPersonality.ambition: Print a town paper people keep rather than throw away.
islandPersonality.favourite: A new story at the bookshop press

article.headline: The editor whose best source never has anything to report
article.standfirst: Reiko prints the evening paper from a desk in the bookshop. Officer Mori supplies the news, when there is some.

article.quote: Nothing happened today is also news. It just needs a better headline.

The incident report, page three: lunch.

name: Officer Mori
bio: Officer Mori walks Main Street after dark, writes everything down and still cannot get the cat to respect him.
backstory: Mori takes the ordinary safety of the streets seriously. His night patrol is slow and exact: Main Street, the seawall, the lanes behind the shops, a look in on an elderly neighbour on the way back to the kōban. He wants the streets to feel safe without feeling watched. His reports are three pages long and supply Reiko’s evening paper with more detail than incident. The cat outside Sakura declines to acknowledge his authority, a long-running difficulty he records conscientiously. The drink-driving notice at Minato is his. He put it up himself and then, off duty, sat under it with a beer. He walked home. He would like that to be in the paper too, as an example.
dailyLife: No suspicious activity today. Except someone teaching the cat to ignore me.

islandPersonality.title: A considerate watchman
islandPersonality.habit: Checks on an elderly neighbour on the way back to the kōban.
islandPersonality.ambition: Make the streets feel safe without making them feel watched.
islandPersonality.favourite: A quiet patrol through Main Street

name: Harbour master
bio: Cargo, ferries, a changing forecast and a lunch delivered by okamochi: a day at the harbour office.
backstory: He checks the tide board before the radio forecast and his knees before either. The harbour office desk holds the manifests, the passenger lists and the timetable that the duty clerk reads aloud whenever anyone rings from Minato’s pink telephone. At noon Mrs Sato arrives with two bowls in her aluminium delivery box. She delivers to the harbour only, which he takes as a professional courtesy and the harbour staff take as a perk of the job. A working harbour teaches patience with tides and with people. When equipment misbehaves he sends for the dock workshop; when a visitor is lost he points them to the right door. The freight book is his as well: every crate on the cargo quay gets a line, and every line gets his initials. He likes watching the morning cargo come in, and he likes it more when it arrives on time.
dailyLife: I can predict rain by my knees. The radio insists on taking all the credit.

islandPersonality.title: Steady as the quay
islandPersonality.habit: Checks the tide board before the radio forecast.
islandPersonality.ambition: Keep the island supplied through any weather.
islandPersonality.favourite: Watching the morning cargo come in

article.headline: The harbour master trusts the tide board more than the radio
article.standfirst: Cargo, ferries, a changing forecast and a lunch delivered by okamochi: a day at the harbour office.

name: Bus driver
bio: He drove the Harbour Line bus for twelve years, until the line became a ferry. The town still calls him the bus driver, and he still keeps the old timetable.
backstory: When the Harbour Line became the ferry he did not want to give up the route. He sat his deck licence on the cargo boats out of Naha, came home as her mate, and has been master of the Minato Maru since 1994. He is aboard by a quarter past seven and ashore after the last call. He brings her alongside from the port wing, where he can see the pier, with Ms Uezu forward on the bow line and Mr Fujita on the quay to take it. Mr Nakandakari, the relief engineer, says he runs her engines too hard. He says the timetable runs them. Ms Ganaha at the ticket window has to explain any late departure, and makes sure he hears about it. He still notices who is carrying groceries, who has missed lunch and who just wants a little company on the crossing, and he knows the regulars by the way they wave from the quay. At seven he takes the day’s log to the harbour master, an old friend, and they read it over the harbour clock. Grandmother Higa’s husband drove the island bus for thirty years. She can still tell the ferry is late by its whistle. He considers that the highest standard in his profession, and keeps time accordingly.
dailyLife: I collect passengers and opening sentences. The best stories start on the last crossing.

islandPersonality.title: Collector of stories
islandPersonality.habit: Knows the regulars by the way they wave from the quay.
islandPersonality.ambition: Keep every call on time, and the island connected to the harbour.
islandPersonality.favourite: The last crossing in golden light

Ms Ganaha at the ticket window has to explain any late departure, and makes sure he hears about it.

He still notices who is carrying groceries, who has missed lunch and who just wants a little company on the crossing, and he knows the regulars by the way they wave from the quay. At seven he takes the day’s log to the harbour master, an old friend, and they read it over the harbour clock.

Grandmother Higa’s husband drove the island bus for thirty years. She can still tell the ferry is late by its whistle. He considers that the highest standard in his profession, and keeps time accordingly.

photos.caption: The last crossing of the day.
Mind the step. Mind the ramp.

name: Grandmother Chinen

islandPersonality.title: The lane’s weather station
islandPersonality.habit: Sweeps the lane in front of her gate at half past six, whatever the weather.
islandPersonality.ambition: See the old house stand through one more typhoon season.
islandPersonality.favourite: The breeze at her gate at three in the afternoon

bio: Tetsuo’s mother keeps a ground-access home at 5 Kitahama, close enough for her son to visit on foot.
backstory: Grandmother Chinen remembers the red-tile house on Kitano-jima, but her home is now 5 Kitahama in Minato. Its level entrance and clear walking route matter more than a grand address. She sweeps by her gate in the morning, tends her plants and keeps a pot ready for Tetsuo. He can visit from his workshop without waiting for a boat, and still eats like he is fifteen. Thuan brings day-old bread from Sakura. Johansson is the ferry’s chief engineer; he and Thuan keep their shared home across the water. Chinen has opinions about his hours, but no longer watches for him at the end of the tropical lane.

name: Miss Higa
role: Schoolteacher; keeps the Umi-no-yu bandai in the evenings and at weekends
place: The island school and the Umi-no-yu bandai

islandPersonality.title: Teacher by day, keeper of the bandai by night
islandPersonality.habit: Marks the class’s homework at the bandai between customers.
islandPersonality.ambition: Send every pupil in her class on to the mainland high school able to read, reckon and swim.
islandPersonality.favourite: The rock bath after dark, once the boiler is running sweet

bio: Miss Higa teaches the island school until half past three. From five she takes your coins at Umi-no-yu, and she still notices who has not done their homework.
backstory: The island school is one room and one small mixed class, and Miss Higa teaches all of it. Vy asks the most questions. Riku talks, and is moved to the front row every week. Mai keeps the class rabbit, which is the best-behaved pupil and knows it. Miss Higa is twenty-nine, marks until five, and then walks down to the bath. The bandai is a raised seat by the door of Umi-no-yu, the island’s bathhouse. From up there you can see over the counter, which is the point of a bandai. Three hundred yen, swimwear in the bath, please: it is a family bath. In the evenings and at weekends she keeps it, with the marking on her knee and the crossword under the marking. The bath is her grandmother’s, and so is the opinion that Miss Higa should be married by now. Grandmother Higa says it at breakfast and again over supper. Her elder brother, the ferry’s oiler, says nothing at all and grins, which is worse. After hours Tetsuo comes to tend the boiler and the pumps. He fixes things; she does the till and pretends not to watch. He takes longer over the pressure gauge than any gauge needs. Neither of them has said a word about it, and the whole of Nishi-machi is waiting.

The boiler is fixed. She was not watching.

name: Grandmother Higa
role: Owner of Umi-no-yu and Higa Liquor
place: Higa Liquor, Umi-no-yu and her Nishi-machi verandah
bio: She owns the bath and the liquor shop, and she knows the ferry by its whistle. From her verandah in Nishi-machi she keeps an eye on the rest.
backstory: Sit a moment, she says, and you will. Grandmother Higa offers a seat, an observation about Sakura, and practical advice on preparing a house for typhoon season, in that order. She keeps the counter at Higa Liquor in the morning and the bandai at Umi-no-yu in the afternoon. Every bottle on the island, at Sakura, Minato or Sato Ramen, came through her door first. Her granddaughter teaches the island school and keeps the bandai in the evenings. Grandmother Higa would like her married, and says so. She has noticed that Tetsuo, who keeps her boiler running for a bath and his supper, takes his time over the pumps. She sends him through the front way, past the bandai, on purpose. Grandmother Sakurai bathes an hour before her. They have been rivals since primary school, and neither has ever let the other win a thing: not a bazaar, not a sports day, not a single argument about the price of rice. Mr Fujita soaks his back every morning and tells her the water is never hot enough. She tells Dr Kakazu the same about his advice on her blood pressure. When the Minato Maru is late she hears it in the whistle, and her grandson, who oils the ferry’s engines, hears about it at supper.

islandPersonality.title: A living island memory
islandPersonality.habit: Pauses at the same shady wall on her morning walk.
islandPersonality.ambition: Teach the children the stories behind the island’s old place names.
islandPersonality.favourite: The village shade after lunch

That is not a shallot.

name: Mr Ōshiro
bio: Mr Ōshiro built his boat from Yakushima cedar. He still scrapes and tars her by hand, and he still goes out before the auction.
backstory: The cedar came from Yakushima before you could not get it any more. He built her in 1968 and will tell you, if you ask, the difference between a repair and a replacement. Most mornings he takes her out with Kōji, his crewman, and they are in before the auction calls. In the afternoons Kōji comes back to the yard to help with the tar. Kōji recommends fibreglass. He has recommended it every season. Mr Ōshiro sees no reason to replace something that has carried him this far, and says so while Kōji bails. Fourth place in the 1979 sabani race remains, in his view, a perfectly respectable subject for conversation. Mr Fujita, who also raced that year, brings it up whenever they meet, and never mentions where he came himself. His yard on the water is a place to stand and watch patient hands. Mr Higa Jr served his time here on sabani and outboards before he went to the ferry, and still comes back to borrow a clamp.

islandPersonality.title: Patient master
islandPersonality.habit: Runs a thumb over the cedar grain before beginning work.
islandPersonality.ambition: Sail his sabani in one more island race.
islandPersonality.favourite: The boatyard on a calm morning

Back before the auction, with his crew.

name: Mrs Kinjō
place: Rainflower Florist, Harbour Park’s Sakura entrance
bio: Mrs Kinjō sells island-grown stems from half past eight, dresses the town for every festival, and keeps a careful eye on the town’s flowers.
backstory: Buckets of fresh stems, leafy pots and hand-made wreaths fill the Rainflower flower stand at Harbour Park’s Sakura entrance. The morning stems come in at half past eight; by the afternoon she is out on deliveries. Thuan comes after closing, and the bouquets for Sakura’s counter are chosen with care on both sides. She is the town’s decorator as well as its florist. The bunting at the harbour, the paper lanterns at Minato and the flowers on Thao’s counter are all arranged by her. Thao says the lanterns cost more than the sake. Mrs Kinjō says that is because the lanterns last. She trades lunch visits with Mrs Nakamura at the Nakamura counter. Their old argument about whose queue was longer has survived the florist’s move to the park. On Sundays she takes tea with Grandmother Sakurai, an old friend, and they agree about almost everything except Grandmother Higa. She wraps everything in plain brown paper, because the flowers should be the bright part.

islandPersonality.title: A grower of small joys
islandPersonality.habit: Turns every bouquet once to check it looks kind from all sides.
islandPersonality.ambition: Fill Rainflower Lane with flowers grown on the island.
islandPersonality.favourite: Her flower-shop doorway after watering

A bouquet for Sakura’s counter.

name: Mrs Nakamura
bio: Mrs Nakamura has the beans on at six, the ice-cream counter open at three and the community kitchen’s andagi in the fryer whenever the town needs feeding.
backstory: Kintoki beans, cooked since six. The ice comes from the plant on the quay, and the old shaving machine roars like a tractor; she trusts its work completely. There has been zenzai on this corner since 1972, and she has no plans to stop. At three she serves the Blue Coral ice cream from the same Nakamura frontage for the school crowd. Her daughter Mai arrives at half past with Vy, her best friend, and the pink guava scoop is already set aside. Mrs Nakamura is bringing Mai up on her own, and does it the way she does everything, early and without fuss. She also runs the community kitchen. When there is a festival, a funeral or a typhoon, the andagi come from her fryer, by the hundred. Mrs Kinjō comes over from the park’s flower stand for lunch and asks how the ice-cream queue is doing. Mrs Nakamura gives her a second bowl and does not move the queue.

islandPersonality.title: Keeper of sweet comforts
islandPersonality.habit: Remembers who wants extra beans in their zenzai.
islandPersonality.ambition: Keep the shop’s summer recipe in the family.
islandPersonality.favourite: The shaded bench outside her shop

article.quote: Zenzai is not fast food. Sit down.

photos.caption: Welcome! Zenzai?
Half past three: two ice creams, one of them guava.

name: Mr Shimabukuro
bio: Mr Shimabukuro minds the power house. Every light on the island comes through his engine room.
backstory: Hear that? Two diesels, one running, one resting. Mr Shimabukuro listens to the generators the way a doctor listens to a chest, and he hears a fault before the meters show it. The second set is to be overhauled before typhoon season; the town assembly minutes say so, and so does he, at length. Postman Tōma brings his parcels to the power house door. They are usually spare parts. Tetsuo comes over when the switchboard needs a second pair of hands, and they talk about the island’s load as other men talk about the weather. On Sunday mornings he fishes off the seawall with Chin at dawn. Who caught the bigger one is a question that has run for years.

islandPersonality.title: The careful keeper
islandPersonality.habit: Listens to the generators before checking the meters.
islandPersonality.ambition: Keep the island’s lights on through the typhoon season.
islandPersonality.favourite: Fishing with Chin on a Sunday morning

article.headline: Two diesels, one running, one resting: the man who keeps the lights on
article.standfirst: Mr Shimabukuro minds the power house. Every light on the island comes through his engine room.

photos.caption: Listening to the engines.
One running, one resting.

name: Kōji
bio: Kōji is up at half past four for the auction and asleep by noon. In between he sorts the catch, loads the ice and would like you to take the tuna head. It is free.
backstory: Before the auction he crews Mr Ōshiro’s sabani, and hears again why she will never be fibreglass. By half past four he is on the auction floor sorting the catch. What the buyers leave goes to Mrs Sato for her stock pot or to the freezer, and Kōji has it sorted before most of the street is awake. At nine he moves to the ice plant and loads the boats for the next night. At noon he goes home to sleep. On Ms Uezu’s week off he works the Minato Maru’s deck as her relief, and he says the ramp is the only thing on the island heavier than a tuna. He is married to Nhung, who sells books and says he smells of fish. He says she smells of books. Their son Riku wants to come out on the boat. He may, Kōji says, when he can swim to the buoy. He likes practical food. He would especially like you to try tuna-head soup.

islandPersonality.title: The keen-eyed sorter
islandPersonality.habit: Can spot a mixed crate before it reaches his sorting bench.
islandPersonality.ambition: Earn the crews’ trust as the island’s best catch sorter.
islandPersonality.favourite: The moment the morning catch is laid out

photos.caption: After the auction.
Supper at home. Still offering the tuna head.

name: Postman Tōma
bio: Postman Tōma walks his round at 10:30 and 16:30, and meets the evening boat for the mailbag. He does not read postcards. The pictures are very nice.
backstory: The plate on the postbox says 10:30 and 16:30, and Tōma trusts it even on the days he doubts himself. Letters for the Ōshiros, a parcel for Mr Shimabukuro at the power station, a postcard for Sakura from somebody in Hanoi. Letters give him a different map of the island, made of names and remembered doorways. Shopkeepers give him news between parcels, and Reiko gets most of it back by teatime. Officer Mori has asked him, more than once, not to lean his bicycle on the koban’s line. At five he takes the evening mailbag at the Port Terminal. Ms Ganaha sells the tickets there. He lingers at her window longer than any mailbag needs; she is busy, and says so, and has not yet asked him to leave. He does not read postcards. He will admit that some of the pictures are very nice.

islandPersonality.title: The cheerful messenger
islandPersonality.habit: Rings his bicycle bell twice at the harbour turn.
islandPersonality.ambition: Deliver every letter before the afternoon heat settles in.
islandPersonality.favourite: A cool drink at Sakura between rounds

The evening mailbag, and a long wait at the ticket window.

name: Riku
place: Island school, the quay and Harbour Park
bio: Riku is nine, Nhung and Kōji’s son, and lives at 3 Kitahama. After school he watches the boats and plays football in Harbour Park.
backstory: Riku lives with his father Kōji at 3 Kitahama. His mother Nhung keeps her room at 1 Front-Row Yard with Reiko, and comes to Kitahama for family supper. Vy is his cousin, and the island school is part of both their days. After school he watches the fishing boats come in. Kōji sorts the catch and sometimes crews the ferry; Riku wants to join him on the boat. He may, his father says, when he can swim to the buoy. Harbour Park has room for football before supper. By half past six he is home at 3 Kitahama, with stories about the quay for Nhung and questions about the boats for Kōji.

islandPersonality.title: The boat watcher
islandPersonality.habit: Watches the boats after school.
islandPersonality.ambition: Swim to the buoy so he can join his father on the boat.
islandPersonality.favourite: Football in Harbour Park before supper

article.headline: After school, Riku is watching the boats
article.standfirst: Riku is nine, Nhung and Kōji’s son, and lives at 3 Kitahama. After school he watches the boats and plays football in Harbour Park.

photos.caption: Watching the boats after school.
Asking the harbour master about the next boat.

name: Vy
place: Island school, Nakamura’s Blue Coral counter and Harbour Park
bio: Vy is eleven and lives with Thao and Chin at 1 Kitahama. After school she meets Mai for a Blue Coral ice cream at Nakamura, then takes her homework to Harbour Park.
backstory: Vy is eleven, Thao and Chin’s daughter, and lives at 1 Kitahama. Her aunt Thuan keeps a weekday room there, and her cousin Riku lives at 3 Kitahama. The island school fills her morning; after class she has plans of her own. Her first stop after school is the Blue Coral counter at Nakamura, where Mrs Nakamura keeps the pink guava scoop aside for her. Mai arrives at the same counter. The lady says this is good customer service. Vy says it is a contract. Then she opens her satchel at a Harbour Park bench, spreads out her homework and does the hard half first, or says she will. When she is thinking she counts the pleats in her skirt. When she is not, she is watching the jan-ken-pon games in Harbour Park and keeping score for the three sisters, who all claim to be winning. She would like to be a ferry captain, or a translator, or both on alternate days.

islandPersonality.title: The rule maker
islandPersonality.habit: Counts the pleats in her skirt when she is thinking.
islandPersonality.ambition: Pass the kanji test without the last ten characters.
islandPersonality.favourite: The pink guava Blue Coral ice cream
